symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern)
Lower and older leaves showing symptoms first
Yellow halo surrounding the circular leaf lesions
Premature leaf drop causing sunscald on fruits
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal pathogen Alternaria solani thriving in warm temperatures (24-29°C) and high humidity or frequent rainfall.
preventionTips: Practice 3-year crop rotation avoiding Solanaceae family (potato, eggplant, pepper)
Ensure adequate plant spacing for vigorous air circulation
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers to keep foliage dry
Mulch the soil bed around tomato plants to prevent soil-borne spore splash
organicTreatment: Apply cold-pressed Neem Oil spray (5ml per liter of water with mild organic soap)
Foliar spray with Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide
Copper-based organic fungicide (Bordeaux mixture 1%) at first sign of spots
chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0g per liter water as protective foliar spray
Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1.0ml per liter water for curative control
Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0g per liter with 7-day pre-harvest interval
Tomato___Early_blight.expertAdvisoryNotes: Early intervention is critical. Remove infected lower leaves immediately and dispose of them away from the field. Do not compost diseased foliage.

symptoms: Irregular water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems
White, fuzzy fungal growth on undersides of leaves during humid mornings
Rapid collapse and browning of entire foliage
Brown greasy lesions on tomato fruits
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans favored by cool, foggy, wet weather (15-22°C with humidity > 90%).
preventionTips: Plant certified disease-free and resistant hybrid varieties
Avoid planting tomatoes near potatoes or downwind from potato fields
Prune lower suckers to maintain canopy ventilation
organicTreatment: Preventative copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride 50 WP sprays
chemicalTreatment: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.0g per liter water
Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1.0g/L water during high disease pressure
Tomato___Late_blight.expertAdvisoryNotes: Late blight can destroy an entire field within 7-10 days if unchecked. Spray systemic fungicides immediately upon early warning.

symptoms: Small, dark, angular, water-soaked leaf spots
Yellow haloes developing around old lesions
Rough, scab-like, raised dark spots on green tomato fruits
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium Xanthomonas, transmitted via infected seeds, splashing rain, and mechanical cultivation during wet weather.
preventionTips: Use hot-water treated certified seeds (50°C for 25 minutes)
Avoid working in tomato fields when leaves are wet
Disinfect pruning tools and farm equipment with 10% sodium hypochlorite
organicTreatment: Copper sulfate formulation with lime (Bordeaux mixture)
chemicalTreatment: Streptocycline (antibiotic) @ 0.5g + Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5g per 10 liters water
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.expertAdvisoryNotes: Bacterial infections cannot be cured with standard fungal sprays. Ensure bactericide application before rainfall.

symptoms: Foliage shows uniform deep green coloration with no visible necrotic spots, yellowing, or wilt.
Tomato___healthy.cause: Optimal plant health and balanced nutrition.
preventionTips: Maintain regular soil moisture and avoid water stress
Apply balanced N-P-K fertilizer and micronutrients (calcium, magnesium, boron)
Monitor weekly for early signs of aphids or whiteflies
organicTreatment: Routine preventative spray of Panchagavya or seaweed extract (3ml/L) to strengthen plant immunity.
Tomato___healthy.expertAdvisoryNotes: Plant is currently healthy. Continue standard fertigation and crop scouting.

symptoms: Target-board dark circular spots with concentric rings on foliage
Yellowing and senescence of infected leaflets
Sunken, dry, leathery brown rot on potato tubers
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Alternaria solani fungus overwintering in infected plant debris and soil.
preventionTips: Plant certified certified seed tubers
Ensure adequate nitrogen nutrition as nutrient-stressed plants are more susceptible
Destroy crop residue after harvest
Potato___Early_blight.expertAdvisoryNotes: Apply protective fungicide when the crop canopy closes across rows.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions starting from leaf tips and margins
White downy fungal mildew on leaf undersides in high humidity
Foul-smelling decay and rotting of tubers in the field and storage
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans, known historically for the Irish Potato Famine.
preventionTips: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini)
Hill up soil well over developing tubers to prevent spores washing into the soil bed
organicTreatment: Foliar compost tea or cow urine extract spray (10%)
Potato___Late_blight.expertAdvisoryNotes: Follow local agro-meteorological advisories. Immediate action is critical before rainfall.

symptoms: Leaves are healthy, turgid, and free of blemishes, blights, or curling.
preventionTips: Regular earthing-up (hilling) around 30 and 45 days after planting
Maintain optimal soil moisture avoiding water stagnation
organicTreatment: Maintain soil health with well-decomposed Farm Yard Manure (FYM).

symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with gray-white centers and reddish-brown borders
Lesions coalesce causing complete burning and drying of leaf blades
Neck blast causing panicles to break and fail to fill grains
Rice___Leaf_Blast.cause: Fungus Magnaporthe oryzae, highly destructive in rice fields with excess nitrogen and cool night temperatures (20-24°C) with dew.
preventionTips: Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer application; split nitrogen into 3-4 doses
Treat seeds before sowing with carbendazim or Pseudomonas
Maintain optimal field water depth to prevent drought stress
organicTreatment: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment (10g/kg seed) and foliar spray @ 2g/L
Foliar spray with fermented cow urine + neem extract
chemicalTreatment: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g per liter water (standard gold-standard treatment)
Rice___Leaf_Blast.expertAdvisoryNotes: Rice blast can reduce paddy yield by up to 50-70%. Spray Tricyclazole at the first appearance of leaf spots and again at panicle emergence.

symptoms: Small, circular to oval dark brown spots on leaf blades and glumes
Spots have yellowish halos resembling sesame seeds
Poor grain filling and discolored paddy grains
Rice___Brown_Spot.cause: Bipolaris oryzae fungus, often associated with nutrient-deficient or water-stressed soil (silicon/potassium deficiency).
preventionTips: Improve soil fertility by applying balanced potassium and farmyard manure
Avoid severe intermittent drying of soil
Soak seeds in hot water (52-54°C for 10 min) before nursery sowing
organicTreatment: Foliar application of silica fertilizers (potassium silicate @ 2ml/L)
Rice___Brown_Spot.expertAdvisoryNotes: Soil testing is recommended. Ensure potassium and zinc levels are adequate.

symptoms: Lush green erect leaves with no blast lesions, brown spots, or bacterial blight streaks.
preventionTips: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water during tillering and flowering
Apply recommended zinc sulfate at basal stage
Rice___healthy.expertAdvisoryNotes: Keep monitoring water level and panicle initiation.

symptoms: Angular, water-soaked leaf spots bordered by leaf veins
Black lesions on stems (Black arm phase)
Water-soaked spots on cotton bolls resulting in stained, discolored lint
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.cause: Xanthomonas bacteria spreading via seed infection, rain splashes, and wind.
preventionTips: Delint seeds with concentrated sulfuric acid before sowing
Use certified resistant Bt-cotton cultivars
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest
chemicalTreatment: Streptocycline 1g + Copper Oxychloride 25g in 10 liters of water
Spray twice at 15-day intervals during vegetative growth
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.expertAdvisoryNotes: Early vegetative protection prevents black arm phase which causes stem breakage.

symptoms: Broad, vibrant green leaves with no vein-banding, boll rot, or angular water-soaked lesions.
preventionTips: Install yellow sticky traps for whitefly and jassid pest monitoring
Avoid excessive vegetative growth by timely pinching
organicTreatment: Pheromone traps for pink bollworm monitoring.
Cotton___healthy.expertAdvisoryNotes: Monitor square formation and boll retention.

symptoms: Small, elongated cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture the leaf epidermis exposing powdery brown spores
Severe leaf chlorosis and premature dry-down
Corn___Common_rust.cause: Fungus Puccinia sorghi, favored by moderate temperatures (16-25°C) and high relative humidity.
preventionTips: Plant rust-tolerant maize hybrids
Rotate with non-host legume crops
Corn___Common_rust.expertAdvisoryNotes: Fungicide is generally cost-effective if rust develops prior to silking stage.

symptoms: Large, elongated, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long)
Lesions start on lower leaves and progress upwards
Extensive leaf blighting giving foliage a burned appearance
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Exserohilum turcicum fungus surviving in crop debris during wet, humid weather.
preventionTips: Deep tillage to bury corn residue
Two-year crop rotation with legumes or oilseeds
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.expertAdvisoryNotes: Protect the ear leaf and leaves above the ear during grain fill.

symptoms: Healthy, uniform green arching leaves without rust pustules or cigar-shaped blights.
Corn___healthy.cause: Optimal crop nutrition and growing conditions.
preventionTips: Ensure adequate nitrogen and zinc nutrition.
